title: POC scoping: KiteWorks workload profile & SLA benchmarking
summary: Initial POC scoping to capture KiteWorks production traffic profile: target QPS, concurrency, token distributions and SLA/benchmark success criteria. Discussed replay dataset, VPC constraints, KMS, and an initial two-week benchmark plan with tail-latency and cost KPIs.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-03
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 57 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Alex Moreno (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Daniel Cho (CTO - KiteWorks), Maya Singh (SRE), Oliver Park (ML Engineer)

[00:00] Alex: hey everyone, uh thanks for joining. i'm alex from redwood, and with me is priya who will lead the deep side of the traffic modeling. can you hear okay?
[00:06] Daniel: yeah we're good. thanks alex. we've been looking forward to this.
[00:12] Alex: great. quick agenda — align on current prod patterns, capture qps/concurrency and token mix, decide replay dataset and success criteria for the poc, and then outline timeline. priya, take it away for signals?
[00:25] Priya: sure. so from our side we need three things: a sample of request logs (headers, latencies, token counts), a replay tool or snapshot, and a rough SLA target. from our experience with similar customers we usually segment traffic into interactive short prompts (~50-150 in tokens), medium form (200-800), and long generation (800+). often tail latency comes from the long ones but the bulk qps is short prompts.
[00:48] Oliver: that's us too. ~70% of calls are the short interactive ones. our mean input tokens is about 35, mean output ~60, but then we have spikes — batch jobs that produce 2k+ output tokens for report generation, maybe 5% of calls but they blow out your GPU cache.
[01:10] Priya: right, that's important. for sizing we need QPS distribution across those classes and peak concurrency. daniel, can you share current numbers?
[01:20] Daniel: sure. our steady-state qps is 18 QPS globally, peaks up to 220 qps for short windows — a 90th percentile daily spike. concurrency is weird because we front a lambda-style proxy, so at the model level concurrency hits ~46 concurrent requests during those spikes.
[01:38] Alex: okay so 18 steady, 220 burst, concurrency ~46 observed at model boundary. what's token distribution at peak vs steady?
[01:47] Oliver: steady window: input 25-40 tokens, output 40-75. peak window it's still short prompts but the long reports run independently — during off-hours they run parallel, like concurrency 12-15 for long jobs. long jobs are 2k-6k output tokens.
[02:08] Maya: one note on data, we can't share raw PII logs. we can produce anonymized payloads with token counts and timing. also we're behind a VPC, and KMS is mandatory for keys.
[02:20] Priya: that's fine. we can accept anonymized replays and work with your security team on KMS integration for the private deployment. question: are you planning hosted redwood or private vpc for the poc?
[02:33] Daniel: given compliance, we want a private VPC deployment for the POC. we might later move to dedicated hosted but poc should be private.
[02:40] Alex: noted. private + KMS — we'll bring the Private onboarding checklist.
[02:44] Alex: let's convert these numbers into a benchmark plan. priya?
[02:47] Priya: propose two phases. Phase A: replay steady-state and 90th spike windows to validate latency SLOs and unit cost. Phase B: stress run with synthetic long generations to exercise memory/kv cache paths and tail latency. For metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency for token generation (end-to-end and model step), tokens/sec, average cost per 1k tokens, and error/retry rates. Also track KV cache hit rates and GPU utilization.
[03:16] Daniel: what's a realistic SLA we should target for p95? we currently aim for p95 < 750ms for short prompts in prod.
[03:24] Priya: for short prompts (<=150 tokens) p95 under 600ms is attainable on our dedicated configs, p99 depends on concurrency and batching. for private it'll depend on instance types you can provide — do you have preferred GPUs?
[03:38] Daniel: we're running on GCP with A2-standard and could provision A10 or A100 if needed; procurement needs to sign off.
[03:44] Priya: A10 is fine for baseline, A100 for aggressive tail SLOs. We'll recommend quantization and a batching profile. also we may suggest prefix KV caching for repeated conversational sessions.
[03:58] Oliver: curious — how do you route requests to smaller cheaper variants when load spikes? we want graceful degradation rather than hard errors.
[04:06] Alex: we have smart routing policies: we can route to a cheaper quantized model variant or higher-latency cheaper region. for private, we can still enforce canary fallback to a smaller variant you approve. that will be part of the rollout plan.
[04:20] Maya: security question — audit logs and SSO. we need SAML SSO for console access, and all request/response must be logged to your audit stream and sent to our SIEM. are those supported in Private?
[04:32] Priya: yes, private supports SAML, fine-grained RBAC, and audit log forwarding (syslog/S3). KMS integration for keyring is supported — we'll include the guide.
[04:44] Daniel: good. Back to workload modeling — how will you generate a replay? we have event logs but no replay infra.
[04:51] Priya: we can accept either a HAR-like export with timestamps and token counts or an anonymized CSV with request timestamps, input token length, output token length, and a small payload sample for fidelity. Redwood has a lightweight replayer that drives the model at real timing or sped-up ratio. for the poc we'll probably do a 1:1 timing for steady windows and a 5x-10x accelerated stress run for phase b.
[05:16] Oliver: for long jobs we can include a subset of 250 sample report requests, anonymized.
[05:22] Alex: perfect. let's document the initial KPIs and success criteria.
[05:26] Priya: suggested success criteria: 1) short-prompt p95 <= 600ms for steady and p95 <= 850ms during 90th spike; 2) p99 < 2.5s for short prompts; 3) long job tail-latency p95 < 6s; 4) no more than 3% error/retry increase vs baseline; 5) unit cost per 1k tokens within 20% of target estimate we will provide. if any of these fail we'll iterate on batching and routing configurations.
[06:06] Daniel: 20% cost band is reasonable. can you estimate baseline cost now?
[06:11] Priya: ballpark — depends on instance, quantization, and batch size. we'll give an initial estimate after we see token mix; for budgeting assume $0.15-$0.45 per 1k output tokens for non-quantized A100 setups, quantized runs can drop that substantially.
[06:29] Maya: procurement needs a PO timeline. what's the POC duration you usually run?
[06:34] Alex: typical short POC is 2-4 weeks: 1 week onboard and replay setup, 1 week steady-state replay and tuning, 1 week stress & finalize. since you're on private, allow a few extra days for VPC peering and KMS work.
[06:48] Daniel: we can target 3 weeks. procurement wants high-level milestones.
[06:52] Priya: we'll provide a milestone schedule: Week 0: security review + VPC/KMS, Week 1: replay ingestion & steady baseline run, Week 2: tuning + spike replay, Week 3: stress & final report. If procurement insists, condense to 2 weeks by running tasks in parallel but that increases risk.
[07:13] Oliver: what about concurrency shaping? our frontend may send bursts; can you simulate the lambda fan-out?
[07:19] Priya: yes — we can replay with a concurrency pattern generator that simulates fan-out with user session affinity preserved. we also model cold-start-like scenarios to simulate cache misses.
[07:30] Alex: let's capture specific telemetry we need from you for sizing: 1) 7 days of anonymized request logs or aggregated histograms (timestamps, input/output token counts, latency at proxy layer), 2) current infra (GPU types, memory), 3) expected growth (3 and 12 month QPS forecast), 4) compliance contacts for KMS and network peering.
[07:58] Daniel: we'll assemble that. one more: are you doing continuous batching on the runtime? we have very spiky QPS and small tokens so batching matters for cost.
[08:09] Priya: yes, our runtime uses continuous batching and dynamic batching thresholds. we will instrument batch size distribution, per-token latency, and batching latency overhead. in the report we'll show effective tokens/sec and inferred cost per call.
[08:28] Maya: we also need to ensure the replays don't expose payload content. we will hash actual payloads and provide tokenized counts plus a small synthetic sample per bucket.
[08:38] Priya: that's acceptable. hash or synthetic examples are fine as long as token lengths and distributions are preserved.
[08:45] Alex: let's recap next steps and owners.
[08:48] Priya: i'll take the lead on benchmark design and will create the replay template. alex will send the private onboarding checklist and security docs. daniel's team will provide anonymized logs and confirm GPU availability. we'll schedule the kick-off run after VPC peering.
[09:05] Daniel: sounds good. any blockers from redwood side?
[09:09] Priya: only that we need the logs and an infra contact for peering. alex will include the SSO/KMS guide.
[09:16] Oliver: one more technical — when you report p99 model step latency, do you include tokenization time? we need clarity on end-to-end vs inference-only numbers.
[09:26] Priya: good call. we'll report both: end-to-end (proxy->proxy) and inference-only (model invoke). tokenization will be captured in a separate bucket so you can disambiguate.
[09:38] Alex: any competitors or alternative routes you're evaluating?
[09:41] Daniel: we're also talking to a self-hosted team (FlareOps) and considering an Anthropic endpoint for a couple of chat features. but our priority is consistent latency and private deployment.
[09:52] Alex: understood. we'll include benchmark comparisons to quantized Anthropic-like baselines in the appendix.
[09:58] Priya: ok to confirm dates — can we aim to start onboarding week of April 13th? that gives you a week to gather logs and internal approvals.
[10:07] Daniel: yes april 13th works. procurement will aim to sign the SOW by then.
[10:12] Alex: great. final recap in chat and i'll attach the onboarding packet.
[10:17] Maya: thanks everyone.
[10:19] Alex: thanks all.

[END:09:00-ish — note: transcript stops here but meeting continued Q&A to close.]
next_steps: Redwood to send Private onboarding checklist and SSO/KMS integration guide (Alex) - target Apr 06, 2026
Priya to share replay template and benchmark plan doc (Priya) - target Apr 07, 2026
KiteWorks to provide anonymized 7-day request histogram CSV and sample payload hashes (Daniel/Oliver) - target Apr 10, 2026
Schedule POC kick-off (onboarding + peering) week of Apr 13, 2026 - calendar invite to be set by Alex
